statement: If absorption monotonicity and an acquired upper U give0<=f(wu)<=U<=2epsilon for all suffixes, predicting U/2 on the terminal prefix and every extension has absolute error<=epsilon. A complete finite cover and fresh predictable batches make the guarantee simultaneous.

body: The adaptive route is the executed winner for this scalar prediction task; it returns a prefix predictor rather than the fixed-tape route’s two-state model. Cost depends on an actual finite small-survival cover, not hidden dimension alone. Rare confidence failures are included in unconditional expected cost/termination proofs. Live labels never reset memory; no full transcript, normalized-survivor or physical apparatus claim is inherited. Read the exact supporting statement and its applicable conditions.
